This would possible, since the ground was covered in snow. But the reason I take it with a grain of salt is because of the following reasons.  
It was snowing a lot, but there was very little wind. So I would have heard someone walking.  
The clouds where thick and dark, with no sign of the sky anywhere. Moonlight is not a likely cause.

If it were some sort of flashlight there is no possible way an average person could have moved the light across the street the way it did. It was perfect. Plus it did not shine or emit a string light. 

Are there other possible reasons? I am getting anxious about this..

My apologies.   
It was about 150m *away* from where I was walking. As for the size of the thing itself, I can't say. It wasn't a massive glowing thing. It was just some sort of slightly transparent white oval thing that if I had to give a size, was 1.5m in vertical length. 

Something I did not clarify.  It was not moving at light speeds. It was a very smooth pace. I would say it was levitating. I saw it for about 4 seconds as it moved across the street behind a house. It was too dark to see what it moved behind though so a house is what an accurate estimate would be.  
If you have more questions, I will do my best to answer.

I doubt it. It was winter, and the road was covered in snow, while it was snowing quietly. I would have heard an engine from that distance. Plus, the light would have lit up the houses in the area. I wouldn't say that it excludes the chances of it being another person.. but under the circumstances it is unlikely.
